A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMAudio. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original MMAudio experiments on VGGSound and AudioCaps, ablations, user studies and comparisons with Movie Gen Audio.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds Greatest Hits evaluation and missing-modality ablations.

M1.justification: The flow-matching objective, multimodal transformer, aligned RoPE, ConvMLPs, synchronization module and default missing-modality handling remain unchanged. The new missing-token alternatives are ablations, without replacing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on 244 unseen Greatest Hits videos containing drumstick impacts. Section 3.5.1 also explicitly identifies Clotho, approximately 31 hours, as training data; v1 mentioned only excluding its test set. This changes reported coverage without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments. Greatest Hits extends evaluation to four existing comparators: Frieren, V-AURA, FoleyCrafter and Seeing&Hearing. Newly cited MultiFoley and AV-Link are discussed as related work.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces onset extraction and comparison with annotated events over each Greatest Hits video's first eight seconds, using accuracy, average precision and F1. Appendix D adds controlled missing-token replacement experiments. The established benchmark and user-study protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a model-free check of synchronization that addresses possible DeSync metric bias, accompanied by spectrogram examples. Appendix D tests sensitivity to default, entirely learnable and zero-filled missing modalities. Existing architectural and training-data ablations remain.

E5.justification: Tables A1 and A2 retain the same user-study means, standard deviations and participant counts. The new experiments report point estimates without adding seed information, uncertainty intervals or formal significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: New results include Greatest Hits F1 of 0.7928 for MMAudio-S-16kHz versus 0.6550 for Frieren, and Table A3's missing-modality comparisons. Matched VGGSound, AudioCaps, user-study, Movie Gen Audio and existing ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(6) and (A1)-(A6), covering flow matching, conditioning, gating, synchronization features and RoPE visualization, are retained. No new formal assumptions, proofs or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims about multimodal joint training, synchronization, efficient state-of-the-art video-to-audio synthesis and competitive text-to-audio performance. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 discusses possible DeSync bias, misleadingly high AP with few generated onsets, and network adaptability to missing-token representations. Appendix H newly acknowledges train/test duplicate videos with different IDs that existing filtering misses. Earlier speech limitations and Movie Gen interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix H newly specifies batch size 512, weight decay 1e-6 and visual-sample duplication factors of five, or three for medium/large models. These are additional disclosures, not demonstrated changes to existing runs. v2 states model availability, whereas v1's introduction promised public release.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to MultiFoley, AV-Link, scale-adapted positional embeddings and the Greatest Hits source paper. Section 2 discusses MultiFoley's similar formulation and relates aligned RoPE to concurrent positional-embedding work. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 prefixes the title with MMAudio, edits wording throughout, expands training explanations and inserts Appendices C and D. Existing appendix sections are renumbered, while the main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2, Table A3 and Figure A8. Existing figures and tables are retained with resizing, repositioning and page reflow; the depth-ablation rows are reordered without changing their values.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 strengthens synchronization evidence through model-free onset evaluation, tests missing-modality choices and supplies useful training details. Its disclosure of residual duplicate-video leakage improves transparency, although that problem remains unresolved. These are meaningful, bounded gains in validation and reproducibility; the established method and results remain unchanged.
